static_traits.name: Li Mingxuan
static_traits.family_status: Good family support: Mother is a dentist, has two sisters.
static_traits.social_status: Interactions with colleagues affected by a pessimistic view of one's own skills; High family support.
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness, no history of similar psychological issues or treatment.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic, highly cooperative, able to self-Reflect with some insight.

basic_info.main_problem: I tend to negate the positive aspects of my baking skills, focusing only on mistakes and failures. This negative thinking pattern appeared after a three-layer cake baking mishap last week. Since then, I have been overly harsh on my baking ability, firmly believing I can never again make a perfect cake; these thoughts arise with every baking attempt, causing Self-doubt and frustration, and affecting Work and interactions with colleagues.
basic_info.core_demands: I have noticed that my negative thinking patterns are affecting my passion for baking and my overall well-being, so I am seeking counseling to gain support and guidance.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / I will fail

special_situations.event: Failed making a three-layer cake for a special order last week (uneven layers, poor appearance)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one creation fails, it proves I can never make complex cakes well and am not suited for baking
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly remakes the same cake to prove oneself, demanding 'must be perfect' by absolutist standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never make three-layer cakes well / I am no good

special_situations.event: Before starting each new baking task, recalls the failure of the three-layer cake
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I try again, the result will be just as bad
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Procrastinates or hesitates to start, or over-monitors details after starting, causing tension
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time will also be botched / will definitely fail

special_situations.event: Successfully baking a batch of cookies
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only making complex perfect cakes counts as success; simple products do not count as achievements
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Belittling or ignoring positive experiences, not recording or consolidating them
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This does not count as success; the cookies were too simple

special_situations.event: At work, checks finished product quality and recalls previous failures
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot get it right every time, it means I cannot do anything well
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Stares only at flaws and mistakes, ignoring overall completion and strengths
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot do anything right in the kitchen

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized through works, to be seen as competent and valuable
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and being negated, worrying about losing one's sense of worth for not being perfect
defense_goal: Uses self-criticism and high standards to control risk and avoid failing again and feeling shame
Maintaining 'caution' by negating positive experiences, avoiding letting one's guard down

object_relations.object_representation: A harsh critic (critical of others or an inner critic)

object_relations.self_representation: A young person needing support and encouragement

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing or recalling the three-layer cake failure, or facing complex baking tasks
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: One failure means 'completely no good'; trying again will only embarrass oneself again
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using absolutist words (e.g. 'never' 'completely') for self-blame, magnifying mistakes, lowering self-evaluation and vocal energy.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others or the counselor invite focusing on recent successes or positive evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Acknowledging success equals ignoring problems and lowering vigilance
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gives seemingly reasonable explanations to belittle success (e.g. 'the task was too simple'), weakening the positive meaning.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When needing to evaluate work quality or make success/failure judgments
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Either perfect or failure; there is no middle ground
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using black-and-white evaluations, insisting on 'must / can only' expressions, refusing to acknowledge partial success.

manifestations: Enjoyment of beloved baking has declined, hard to enjoy it as in the past
Self-doubt Reinforcement, shaken sense of achievement and worth
outcomes: Reduced motivation and increased Sense of frustration

manifestations: Bound by the inner rule of 'must make a perfect cake'
Hesitating to try for fear of failing again
outcomes: Rising Anxiety and tension, declining performance

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent self-blame in sessions and at Work, using absolutist expressions like 'never / no good'
Excessively cares about possible mistakes, overly cautious to the point that performance is limited

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizes 'must make a perfect cake to count as success' as an absolute standard
Negating the success of simple tasks like cookies, treating them as 'not counting'

exception_events.target_problem: When recalling the three-layer cake failure and starting to bake, the client usually Anticipates failure, with Decreased attention and Self-doubt, thereby affecting the quality of the work.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last week there was a cookie-baking experience of 'doing quite well'; unlike usual, the finished product was satisfactory that time, and the experience was relatively positive.
exception_events.reason: Clue: lower task difficulty (cookies are relatively less complex than three-layer cakes), thereby reducing tension and failure Anticipation, making it easier to concentrate.

positive_force: Good family support (Mother and two sisters can provide help and guidance)
Has self-Reflection ability, able to identify the pattern of 'self-fulfilling prophecy'
Willing to try recording positive experiences and cognitive restructuring (agrees to write a log of successes/challenges in parallel)
Has persistence and drive (tried many times to remake the cake)
There are visible successful experiences (such as successfully baking cookies)
negative_force: Significant negative cognitive patterns (negating the positive, mental filtering, overgeneralization, predicting the future, black-and-white thinking)
Perfectionism / all-or-nothing standards reinforcing failure Fear
Excessive self-criticism, prone to equating one failure with total incompetence
Failure Anticipation causing tension and Decreased attention, further interfering with performance
Tendency to belittle positive evidence, weakening Self-efficacy

target_behavior.behavior: Strong failure Anticipation and Self-doubt arising in baking tasks, with scattered attention.
antecedent: Before starting a new baking task, recalls the three-layer cake failure
Facing more difficult or complex baking requirements (such as a three-layer cake)
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing failure and 'all-or-nothing' standards, with overgeneralization leading to negative inferences about the stability of one's abilities.
target_behavior.function: Psychologically avoiding potential failure and shame, trying to gain a sense of control through self-defense.
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired performance, more mistakes, Decreased job satisfaction, and affected interactions with colleagues and self-esteem.

target_behavior.behavior: Negating positive results (treating successful experiences as 'not counting').
antecedent: When a smoother baking result occurs (e.g. cookies succeed)
Being reminded to focus on positive evidence or small progress
target_behavior.core_reason: Perfectionist standards and mental filtering, believing only complex works that are perfectly flawless count as success.
target_behavior.function: Maintaining consistency with the inner negative schema, avoiding facing uncertainty or letting one's guard down.
target_behavior.consequence: Damaged Self-efficacy, Decreased motivation, perpetuating the cycle of negative emotions and failure Anticipation.
